tickets.subject: Scheduled reports slowing down the orchestrator after a week of flow history
tickets.description: Redwood University reported that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator started taking much longer to generate scheduled usage reports after the flow history aged past about a week. They said the dashboard felt sluggish during the same window, but edge tunnels and policy forwarding were still up. TAC reviewed the orchestrator and confirmed the reporting job window now overlaps with peak change activity. The issue is isolated to the reporting service on the 3.3 orchestrator.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified this as KB-5107 and applied the documented workaround. We reduced flow-history retention to 5 days with `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed the change, which brought report runtime back to normal and reduced CPU contention during the job window.

tickets.subject: 3.3 orchestrator reports causing long delays and policy lag
tickets.description: Prairie State College called in to report that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator was spending most of the morning running scheduled reports, and administrators noticed policy edits were sometimes delayed until the reports finished. The caller initially suspected a database issue because the graphs were slow to refresh, but the orchestrator services remained otherwise healthy. TAC checked the reporting workload and saw the jobs were running against a large flow-history set. The problem is confined to the reporting process on the 3.3 orchestrator.
tickets.resolution: TAC traced the behavior to KB-5107 and implemented the workaround. We shortened flow-history retention to 5 days using `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed it, then advised the customer to keep larger reports in a smaller time window or schedule them during low-change periods.

tickets.subject: Reporting jobs on Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 taking 20+ minutes
tickets.description: BlueRiver Credit Union emailed that overnight reports on their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator had started running far longer than before, and the web dashboard was lagging while the job was active. They also noted no tunnel outages and no obvious alarm on the edges. TAC confirmed the orchestrator was on 3.3 and observed sustained high CPU in the reporting service during the scheduled run. The job behavior matched a reporting scalability issue rather than a general platform failure. The orchestrator log showed '%ERR-ORCH-5178' during the report window.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-5107 and applied the documented mitigation. We set `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed the change to reduce the amount of data each report must process, which restored acceptable report times.

tickets.subject: Orchestrator CPU spikes when monthly reports run
tickets.description: Summit Logistics escalated that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator became very slow every time the nightly reporting task ran, and the NOC saw administrator actions queue up behind it. They suspected an edge problem at first, but `show sdwan tunnels` on the edges showed normal tunnel state and loss was not changing. TAC confirmed the orchestrator was running 3.3 and that the reporting service was consuming the majority of CPU while the job was active. The symptom pattern matched a known reporting scale limit. The orchestrator log showed '%ERR-ORCH-5178' during the report window.
tickets.resolution: TAC resolved the case per KB-5107 by applying the workaround. We reduced flow-history retention to 5 days with `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed the change, which lowered the reporting workload and removed the CPU contention during scheduled jobs.

tickets.subject: 3.3 report generation slows the management plane
tickets.description: CivicWorks Public Agency reported that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator was still reachable, but report generation had become slow enough to interfere with routine admin work. The on-site engineer initially thought the issue might be tied to a certificate renewal task, but the timing lined up with scheduled reporting and not with any certificate or edge event. TAC checked the orchestrator version and confirmed it was 3.3, with the reporting service running hot while jobs processed a large flow-history set. No tunnel or policy fault was found on the edges. The orchestrator log showed '%ERR-ORCH-5178' during the report window.
tickets.resolution: TAC treated this as KB-5107 and applied the supported workaround. We changed flow-history retention to 5 days using `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed it, which reduced report size and brought the management-plane load back to normal.
